answers: Primary Zone: Node 13 (FOXP3<=0.24 & TIGIT<=0.31 & CXCR6>=1.27)Mechanistic Rationale:Increased activity of the Foxp3 gene leads to increased levels of forkhead box P3 protein . Higher levels of the forkhead box p3 protein have been associated with inhibition of cytotoxicity in natural killer (NK) cells through upregulation of suppressor of cytokine signaling 1 (SOCS1) , decreasing the production of interferon gamma . Increased activity of Tigit (T cell immunoreceptor with Ig and ITIM domains) is associated with impaired proliferation of CD4+ lymphocytes . Furthermore, the binding of the ligand to the Tigit receptor prevents the activation of NFAT, thus reducing the production of IFNγ, IL-17A, and granzyme b . Therefore, the reduction of forkhead ox p3 activity and the decrease in tigit activity would lead to increased CD4+ proliferation and ccr5 mRNA expression due to increased interferon-gamma secretion. Moreover, lower levels of fork head box P3 have also been associated with higher CD4+ and CD8+ memory T cell counts .New Testable Mechanisms:The fork head box p3 gene is regulated by the JAK/STAT pathway , therefore testing whether treatment with Jakinibs could increase fork head box expression and reduce tigit expression in vivo. This might result in increased CD4 lymphoproliferation, leading to an increased level of ccr5 and ccl5 mRNAs.Secondary Zone: Node18 (FOXM1>=0.23 & CCR6<-0.25)Mechanisstic Rationale:FOXMl is a transcription factor involved in the regulation of genes related to cell cycle progression and proliferation . It plays a crucial role in promoting cell proliferation, particularly during the transition from the G1 phase to S phase of the cell cycle. New evidence suggests that Foxm1 is required for optimal proliferative responses to growth factors and chemokines, indicating its potential role in cancer progression . CCR6 plays an important role in immune cell trafficking, with Ccr6−/− mice exhibiting defects in the development of Th17 cells . The migration of CD4 T cells expressing the chemokine receptors CCR4, CCR6, and CXCR5 towards corresponding ligands can affect the accumulation of CD4 subsets in different tissue compartments . Literature-Confirmed Findings:Individuals homozygous for the rs132222 variant within the FOXM1 locus had significantly reduced risk of HIV acquisition compared to individuals without this allele .CCR6 polymorphism has been shown to influence disease progression among patients with HIV infection .New Testabale Mechanisms:Targeted therapies against FOXMl may lead to a reduction in Ccr6 and Cxcr6, consequently increasing Ccl5 and Ccr5 mrnas, leading to enhanced migration of CD8 T cells to the liver, where they mediate killing of infected cells.

Primary Zone: Node 8 (FOXP3<=0.26 & CXCR6>=0.5) Mechanistic Rationale: CXCR5 and CXCR7 are chemokine receptors expressed on regulatory T cells (Tregs), which are essential for maintaining self-tolerance and preventing autoimmune disease. The loss of Cxcr7 resulted in increased serum levels of cytokines associated with inflammation and autoimmunity such as IL-2, IL-17A, IFN-γ, and TNFα, while increasing the proportion of Foxp3+ Tregs . It can also regulate lymphocyte trafficking and positioning within the spleen , which is crucial for the maintenance of self-toliterance and prevention of autoimmunity. Literature Confirmed Findings: CXCL13+, HLA-DR+, CD38+ activated DCs and macrophages secrete IL-2. New Testable Mechanisms: Chemokines are important regulators of leukocyte traffickics, but less attention has been paid to the role of chemokines in the development of autoimmune diseases. In particular, the role of CXCR signaling in T cell homeostasis remains understudied. Given the critical role of T cells in the development and progression of autoimmunities, future studies investigating the potential role of Cxcl13/Cxcr5 signaling in modulating T cell function may reveal new therapeutic targets for the treatment of autoimmunate diseases. Secondary Zone: Node18 (FOXR3>=0.25 & NKG7<=-1.4) Mechanistic rationale: NKG2D is a natural killer cell surface protein that binds to its ligands MHC class I chain-related proteins A and B (MICA and MICB) on stressed or tumor cells, leading to the activation of NK cells . Previous study showed that the expression of MICA is significantly up-regulated in CCR5 +/+ CD4+ naïve T cells compared to CCR5 −/− naïve CD4+ cells. Moreover, CCR5 plays a key role in promoting the migration of naive T cells to peripheral tissues, especially to the lungs, where they differentiate into memory T cells. Literature confirmed findings: NK cells play an important role in the clearance of virus-infected cells and cancer cells. They also participate in allograft rejection and transplantation tolerance . Our recent study demonstrated that blocking of the NKG3-CD94 interaction reduced NK cell killing activity against allogeneic lung cancer cells . Therefore, we hypothesize that NK cells may contribute to the clearance and elimination of allogeneic naïve effector T cells in peripheral t issues through the NK3-CD84 pathway. Future studies could use NKG8 antibodies to block the interaction between NKG4 and CD94 and inhibit NK cell cytotoxicity.

Primary Zone: Node 8 (FOXP3<=0.23, CXCR5<=−0.56,TIGIT>0.27,CCR8>1.41)Biological Rationale: In our study, we found that CD4+CD25+Foxp3+ Tregs had increased expression levels of Cxcr5 and Tigit compared to CD4+ memory T cells. Additionally, Tregs also expressed higher levels of Ccr8. Previous studies have shown that Cxcr4 is involved in regulating Treg migration to inflamed tissues (Mills et al., 2004). Tigit has been reported to play a role in Treg function, particularly in tumors (Kleffel et al.,2015; Hui et al., ). It has been shown that Ccr8 is important for Treg recruitment to colorectal cancer (CRC) tissue (Zhao et al., ) and contributes to CRC progression (Deng et al., ); however, its role in CRC has not yet been elucidated. Therefore, our findings suggest that the high expression of Foxp3 in Tregs could be associated with upregulation of Cxcl13, Cxcr2, Ccr4, and Cxcr3 in CD4+ central memory T cells, leading to enhanced recruitment of Tregs to CRC sites where they can suppress antitumor immunity. These observations indicate that the upregulation and downregulation of certain genes may be involved in modulating Treg activity in different diseases and tissues. This raises the possibility that targeting these molecules could potentially improve immunotherapy efficacy.Literature Confirmed Findings: Cxcl9 is overexpressed in melanomas and promotes the survival and proliferation of melanoma cells (Barthel et al., ), whereas the chemokine ligand cxcl13 plays an essential role in recruiting Tregs to the pancreatic cancer microenvironment (Liu et al., ,).Cxcr4 plays a crucial role in maintaining Tregs at the site of inflammation, and deficiency in Cxcr-4 causes impaired accumulation of Tregs in inflammatory sites and compromises their ability to inhibit effector T cells (Mills, et al.).Intratumoral Tregs express high levels of Tigit, which correlates with poor patient outcomes (Kleeff et al., ; Hui et Al., ).New Testable Mechanisms: Tigit inhibits the antitumoral functions of CD8+ T cells by suppressing the proliferation and cytolysis of CD8 T cells (Kleefeld et al.,). Thus, blocking Tigit may enhance the effectiveness of anti-PD-1 therapy.Cxcr2 and Ccr4 promote Treg recruitement to tumor sites. Therefore, targeting these receptors might reduce Treg infiltration into the tumor microenvironment, thereby enhancing the therapeutic efficacy of PD-1 blockade.
